written: 2026-10-31, before any solve, before any sampling of FL-9 and before any code of this study ran
study: the surface blobs surf3 = (1+x+2x^2) e^-x and surf5 = (1+x+4x^3/3) e^-x, and Cortez's blob, scored on A's helix (FL-9, free space, float64) against the helix reference (3.060 +- 0.147 mm/s preregistered, 3.057 +- 0.057 post hoc; R_xx 5.1955e-5 N s/m; R_x,Ox -2.530e-9 N s), with a quasi-uniform sampling of FL-9's surface in scratch code

method.sampler: MIME's own sampler at a spacing h/3 (about 9 times the target count) thinned to MIME's own count at h by farthest-point selection (Euclidean), then 6 discrete Lloyd steps on the dense set (each sample moved to the dense point nearest its cell's area-weighted centroid); weights are the cells' areas on the dense set. Same count, so the same mean spacing and the same eps at a blob fraction
method.kernels: the blob spike's closed forms (kernels.json), series below rho = 0.5 (float64) or 1.0 (float32); Cortez's as MIME's
method.solve: point forces at the samples, eps = fraction x mean spacing (MIME's rule), the matrix assembled in place, Cholesky, LU where the factor is not finite; R = M^T A^-1 M; the axial speed -R_x,Ox omega / R_xx at 10 Hz
method.orders: observed by self-convergence: three successive levels, U(h) = U0 + C h^p solved for p (the reference's band is too wide to measure an order against)
method.edge_test: the same pipeline on two bodies of FL-9's size: a prolate spheroid (semi-axes 3.735, 1.56, 1.56 mm; no edges; exact axial drag and torque by Chwang & Wu) and a capped circular cylinder (radius 1.56 mm, length 7.47 mm; the caps' edges, no thread; self-convergence). The edges hold the order back if the cylinder's observed order sits with the helix's and below the spheroid's

S1_quality.claim: at 0.16 mm (5,984 samples) the quasi-uniform sampling has nearest-neighbour/h minimum 0.55-0.85 and 5th percentile 0.75-0.95, and under 1% of samples with a neighbour closer than h/2 (MIME's: 26-27%, minimum 0.26)
S1_quality.meaning: above 5% the sampler has failed its purpose and the surface blobs' arms are not scored on it

S2_coverage.claim: the caps' share of samples, and the crest band's (the lateral samples with rho above R(1 + 0.6 modulation)), each within 5% (relative) of their share of the area; samples within h of a cap's rim within 15% of that strip's area share
S2_coverage.meaning: outside, the sampler is uneven by region and the edge test's reading is confounded with it

S3_condition_mime.claim: on MIME's sampling at 0.16 mm: Cortez 0.5 about 3.6e3 (read: the reference measured it); surf3 at 1.0 1e7-1e12; surf5 at 1.5 and above and surf3 at 2.0: 1e12 or more, or the Cholesky factor not finite
S3_condition_mime.meaning: confirms on the helix the spike's sphere finding that MIME's sampling is what makes the surface blobs singular

S4_condition_qu.claim: on the quasi-uniform sampling at 0.16 mm: Cortez 0.5 1e2-2e3; surf3 1.0 2e3-1e5, 1.5 1e5-1e7, 2.0 1e7-1e10; surf5 1.5 1e5-1e7, 2.0 1e7-1e9.5, 2.5 1e9-1e12, 3.0 1e12-1e15 (every factor finite)
S4_condition_qu.meaning: a condition above 1e14 at a fraction makes that arm rounding-limited in float64 and void in float32

C1_sphere_pipeline.claim: the unit sphere on MIME's sampling, 16 x 32 = 512 samples, surf5 at fraction 2, through this pipeline on the GPU: max error over F_z, T_z, F_x, T_x 1.99e-8, the spike's, to 2 digits; Cortez 0.5 4.16e-2
C1_sphere_pipeline.meaning: fails: the kernels or the solve are wrong here and no score is reported

C2_sphere_sampler.claim: the unit sphere on the quasi-uniform sampler at 512 samples, surf5 at fraction 2: max error 2e-9 to 2e-7 (pass: within a factor 10 of the spike's 2e-8)
C2_sphere_sampler.meaning: fails: the sampler's points carry a quadrature error the surface blobs cannot absorb, and no surface-blob score on it is reported

C3_node.claim: Cortez 0.5 on MIME's own sampling at 0.16 mm gives 2.7979 mm/s (the node's), R within 1e-12 of the reference's route (a) record
C3_node.meaning: fails: the FL-9 set-up is not the reference's and no score is reported

P1_cortez_qu.claim: Cortez 0.5 on the quasi-uniform sampling at 0.16 mm: 2.70-2.90 mm/s, its change from 2.798 under 0.10 mm/s; observed order 1-2.3 on both samplings
P1_cortez_qu.meaning: the sampling alone does not close today's blob's -8.9%; its error stays quadrature

P2_surf5.claim: surf5 at fraction 2.0 at 0.16 mm: speed 3.00-3.10 mm/s (inside the reference's band), R_xx within 0.5% of 5.1955e-5, |R_x,Ox| within 2% of 2.530e-9; observed order on R_xx 1-2.5
P2_surf5.meaning: inside the band and order about 1-2: usable but edge-limited; order 4 or more: the edges do not hold it back

P3_surf3.claim: surf3 at 1.5 at 0.16 mm: speed 2.95-3.10 mm/s, R_xx within 1%; at 1.0 the quadrature error shows (speed 2.85-3.05); observed order 1-2.5

P4_fractions.claim: within each surface blob, the larger fractions (surf5 2.5, 3.0; surf3 2.0) are no better than 2.0 / 1.5 at 0.16 mm on the speed, by the edges' larger reach
P4_fractions.meaning: the best fraction on the helix is the smooth body's or below

E1_spheroid.claim: the spheroid of FL-9's size, surf5 at 2.0 on the quasi-uniform sampler: axial drag and torque error under 1e-4 at 0.16 mm, observed order 4 or more; surf3 at 1.5 order 2.5 or more
E1_spheroid.meaning: fails (order under 3): the sampler's quadrature, not the edges, limits the order, and the edge test cannot discriminate

E2_edges.claim: the capped cylinder's observed order for surf5 at 2.0 is 1-2.5, with the helix's, below the spheroid's: the caps' edges hold the order back (the regularised layer's error is O(eps) within about eps of an edge, so O(eps^2) or less on the resistance)
E2_edges.meaning: the cylinder's order 4 or more: the edges do not hold it back, and the helix's order (if low) has another cause

F1_float32.claim: at the best configuration (expected surf5 2.0 at 0.16 mm) float32 gives the speed within 1e-3 relative of float64 (Cholesky finite if the condition is under about 1e7, else LU)
F1_float32.meaning: worse than 1e-2: float32 is void at the surface blobs' fractions on the helix

I5_answer.claim: at matched unknowns (5,984), the best surface blob on quasi-uniform sampling and route (b) (3.064, +0.2%) are both inside the reference's band, so the reference cannot rank them; against the two routes' point values (3.057-3.060, an estimate) route (b) is the closer on the speed and the surface blob the closer on R_xx; at matched A100 wall time the dense surface-blob solve at 5,984 samples (1-3 s) is cheaper than route (b)'s 2.65 M-point solve, which takes 2-4x longer
I5_answer.meaning: the draft's order (lever 1 before lever 3 for the screw's speed) stands unless the surface blob beats route (b) on the speed at matched wall time

COST.claim: one A100-80GB call of 15-35 min, $0.75-1.75, well under the $8.00
